mainTopic: The danger of arrogance and the greatness of humility. Then how a husband's קינוי works, and why a suspected wife whose husband dies must do חליצה rather than יבום.
overview: This amud first finishes a proof that an arrogant person ends up lowered. It reads the צרעת words שאת (height) and ספחת (something attached) as hinting that whoever raises himself up ends up dependent. רבי יהושע בן לוי then teaches that a humble person is counted as if he brought every קרבן, and that his תפילה is never rejected. He also teaches that whoever carefully weighs his ways will see the salvation of הקדוש ברוך הוא. The גמרא then returns to the משנה of כיצד מקנא לה. It points out an apparent contradiction about whether speaking with the man counts as סתירה. אביי resolves it: a 'don't speak' warning means nothing, and only seclusion after a 'don't be secluded' warning forbids her. Next the גמרא asks why such a woman must do חליצה and cannot do יבום. רב יוסף answers from the פסוק 'לאיש אחר', and he and אביי debate why חליצה is still needed. The amud ends in the middle of רב יוסף's reply to אביי's challenge, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading שאת and ספחת as Height and Being Attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a verse-based proof that arrogance leads to being lowered. שאת means 'raised up,' and ספחת means 'attached' or secondary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse about צרעת says 'for a שאת and for a ספחת.' The word שאת always means height, as in the verse about hills that are 'lifted up.' The word ספחת always means something attached, as in the verse 'attach me, please, to one of the כהונה groups to eat bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the previous lines that an arrogant person ends up diminished. It does this by explaining two words from the צרעת verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is proven from another verse. שאת matches 'נשאות' (lifted up), so it means raising oneself up. ספחת matches 'ספחני' (attach me), which describes a lowered family that must attach itself to others to get food. Put together, the order of the words hints that someone who raises himself up will end up dependent and lowered.

steps.title: A Humble Person Is Counted as Bringing Every Offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a humble person is credited as if he offered all the קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Come and see how great humble people are before הקדוש ברוך הוא. When the בית המקדש stood, a person who brought an עולה got the reward of an עולה. One who brought a מנחה got the reward of a מנחה. But a person whose mind is humble is treated by the פסוק as if he brought all the קרבנות together, as it says: 'The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי praises humility. He says a humble person gets credit for every קרבן, not just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He sets up a contrast. A normal קרבן earns only the reward of that one specific offering. The פסוק says 'זבחי אלהים' (sacrifices, in the plural) are a broken spirit. So a humble spirit is worth all the offerings at once.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A humble person is credited as if he brought all the קרבנות.

steps.title: The Humble Person's Prayer Is Never Rejected
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי adds a second reward for the humble: God does not reject his תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but his תפילה is not rejected, as it says: 'A broken and crushed heart, O God, You will not despise.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי adds a second benefit of humility, using the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק taught that humility is worth all the קרבנות. The second half adds that God will not 'despise' a broken heart. This means the humble person's prayers are always accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reward to the teaching in step 2, from the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תפילה of a humble person is not rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: Arrogance (שאת) leads to being lowered (ספחת). Humility, though, is worth all the קרבנות, and it makes one's תפילה accepted.

steps.title: One Who Weighs His Ways Will See God's Salvation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that whoever carefully evaluates his conduct merits seeing God's salvation. He reads the verse with an אל תקרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Whoever weighs his ways in this world merits to see the salvation of הקדוש ברוך הוא. As it says: 'And to one who sets (וְשָׂם) his way, I will show the salvation of God.' Don't read it as וְשָׂם (sets) but as וְשָׁם (weighs) his way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives another teaching about good character. He says that thinking carefully about how you act brings a great reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is written וְשָׂם (with a שׂ), meaning 'sets.' Through an אל תקרי, he reads it as וְשָׁם (with a שׁ), meaning 'weighs' or 'appraises.' So the reward of seeing God's salvation goes to someone who thinks through his actions before he acts.

keyTerms.meaning: One who weighs and evaluates his ways

His salvation
Merits, is worthy of

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate teaching by the same speaker, רבי יהושע בן לוי, also about proper character.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever carefully evaluates his conduct merits seeing God's salvation.

steps.title: The משנה Seems to Treat Speaking as Seclusion
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה of כיצד מקנא לה, the גמרא begins showing a contradiction inside it. The warning is phrased as 'don't speak with him,' which suggests that speaking itself counts as סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'How does he warn her...' This itself is difficult. You said that he tells her in front of two witnesses, 'Do not speak with this man.' That seems to show that speaking counts as seclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the husband's קינוי (warning). It starts pointing out a problem: the wording of the warning makes it sound like just talking with the man is the forbidden act. The other half of the contradiction comes in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's warning is worded 'אל תדברי' (don't speak). This implies that speaking is the act that would make her a סוטה, so speaking would be treated like סתירה. The גמרא is setting this up to clash with the משנה's next line, which says that if she only spoke with him, she is still permitted to her husband.

This itself is difficult (the text contradicts itself)
Apparently, this shows that
Seclusion with the man, which makes a warned woman forbidden to her husband
Speaking

steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the משנה of כיצד מקנא לה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The warning's wording (don't speak) implies that speaking counts as סתירה. This is set up to clash with the משנה's later ruling that speaking alone does not forbid her to her husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the גמרא's effort to define exactly what the husband's warning must forbid. That decides which act makes a warned woman forbidden to her husband.

steps.title: The later line of the משנה says speaking means nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its contradiction: the משנה later says that if she spoke with the man, she is still permitted to her husband and to תרומה, so speaking seems to mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the משנה teaches: if she spoke with him, she is still permitted to her home and still permitted to eat תרומה. So apparently speaking is nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the contradiction it started in step 5. It points to a later line in the same משנה that says speaking with the man changes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, the warning 'don't speak with him' made it sound like speaking itself counts as סתירה. Now the משנה says that after speaking she is still fully permitted. So which is it? Does speaking matter, or not?

keyTerms.meaning: And then it teaches (later in the same source)

phrases.english: and permitted to eat תרומה,

steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה of כיצד מקנא לה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first line implies speaking counts as סתירה; the later line says speaking has no effect. The two lines seem to clash.

steps.title: אביי explains the משנה as a list of combinations
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה matches what the husband warned against with what the wife actually did. A 'don't speak' warning is not a valid warning at all. Only a 'don't be secluded' warning followed by real seclusion forbids her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is what the משנה means. If he said 'don't speak' and she spoke, or 'don't speak' and she secluded herself, it is nothing. If he said 'don't seclude yourself' and she only spoke with him, she is still permitted to her husband and to תרומה. If she went into a hidden place with him and stayed long enough for relations, she is forbidden to her husband and forbidden to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by rereading the משנה as a list of cases. Each case pairs the husband's warning with the wife's action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'don't speak' in the משנה are not a valid warning; they are one of the cases that has no effect. A proper warning is 'don't be secluded,' and even then speaking alone changes nothing. Only actual seclusion long enough for relations, after a 'don't be secluded' warning, makes her forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the text)

steps.whatToRemember: Speaking never matters here. A valid קינוי is 'don't be secluded,' and only real seclusion for כדי טומאה after that warning forbids her.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a 'don't speak' warning plus seclusion forbids her. אביי says that is 'nothing,' because the warning itself was not a proper קינוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as a list of warning-and-action combinations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'don't speak' wording sounded like a valid warning that makes speaking count as סתירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Don't speak' is not a valid warning; only 'don't be secluded' followed by seclusion for כדי טומאה forbids her, and speaking never matters.

steps.title: Why must she do חליצה and not יבום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that if the husband dies, she does חליצה, and asks why she cannot simply marry the brother through יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And if he dies, she does חליצה.' Why? Let her also do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and challenges it. If her husband died, why can't she marry his brother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was only suspected; nobody proved she sinned. So why should she be blocked from יבום? The גמרא wants a source for forbidding her to the brother.

keyTerms.meaning: She does חליצה, the ceremony that frees her from the brother
Marrying the brother of a husband who died without children
Why?

phrases.english: And if he died, she does חליצה.
Why?
Let her also do יבום!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה after closing the warning discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that she does חליצה and not יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She is only under suspicion, so there seems no reason to forbid her to the brother.

steps.title: רב יוסף: 'Another man' but not the יבם
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף learns from the פסוק 'and she becomes another man's' that such a woman may go to another man, but not to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the פסוק says, 'And she leaves his house, and goes and becomes another man's.' Another man, but not the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question with a פסוק. The words 'another man' teach that she cannot marry the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a woman leaving her husband's house and marrying 'another man.' רב יוסף reads 'another' as excluding the brother. So a woman who lost her place with her husband this way cannot go to his brother, and must do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (a proof from a verse)
Another man
The brother of the husband who died, who could do יבום

steps.whatToRemember: From 'לאיש אחר' we learn she may marry someone else, but not the יבם, so she does חליצה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: the verse says:
'And she leaves his house, and goes
and becomes another man's.'
To another man, and not to the יבם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since she is only suspected, she should be allowed יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק permits her only to 'another man,' which excludes the יבם, so she does חליצה.

steps.title: If יבום is ruled out, why is חליצה needed?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: if the פסוק sends her to 'another man' and blocks the יבם, she should not need חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, she should not need חליצה either!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's teaching from the previous step. If the Torah blocks her from the יבם, why tie her to him at all through חליצה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה is the ceremony that releases a widow from her bond to her husband's brother. אביי reasons that if the פסוק already frees her to marry 'another man' and she can never marry the יבם, then there is no bond left to release. So the משנה's demand for חליצה seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: a challenge that pushes someone's logic to an uncomfortable result
The ceremony that frees a childless widow from her bond to her husband's brother
She should need / require

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, who just explained the פסוק in the last step.

phrases.english: But if so,
she should not need chalitza either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's derivation from step 9 by drawing out its consequence.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading that 'another man' excludes the יבם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק releases her to anyone except the יבם, there is no bond to the יבם that needs releasing, so חליצה should not be required.

steps.title: Like a גט: forbidden, yet still bound
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that even when she was forbidden to her living husband she still needed a גט, so now too she needs חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If the husband were alive, wouldn't she need a גט? Now too she should need חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself with a comparison. Being forbidden to someone does not mean the marriage bond is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While her husband was alive she was forbidden to him, yet she still needed a גט to marry someone else. That shows a bond can exist even when living together is forbidden. In the same way, the bond to the יבם remains even though יבום is forbidden, so חליצה is still needed to cut it.

keyTerms.meaning: A bill of divorce
If (in a hypothetical case)
Now

steps.whatToRemember: Being forbidden to a man is not the same as being free of him. She needs a גט from the husband, and in the same way she needs חליצה from the יבם.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רב יוסף is answering אביי.

phrases.english: If the husband were alive,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (a גט while the husband is alive)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If she is forbidden to the יבם, she has no bond to him and needs no חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being forbidden does not cancel the bond. Just as she needed a גט from the husband she was forbidden to, she needs חליצה from the יבם.

steps.title: A second version: she should not destroy the house
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב יוסף's reasoning differently: the פסוק sends her out so she won't ruin the house, so it cannot also tell the יבם to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב יוסף said: The Torah said, 'And she leaves his house and goes and becomes another man's,' so that she not destroy his house. And you say she should also go through יבום?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of how רב יוסף explained the rule. This version gives a reason why יבום is blocked while חליצה stays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about a husband who sends his wife away because he found something improper about her, so that she won't ruin his home. It makes no sense for that same פסוק to tell the יבם to bring her into his home through יבום. This logic only rules out marrying her, not releasing her, so חליצה is still required.

steps.title: Then she should not marry anyone else either
steps.stepSummary: אביי attacks the second version: if the worry is ruining a house, she should not marry another man either, yet the פסוק says she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, she should not marry another man either, so that she not destroy his house! He said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי turns the 'destroy the house' logic back on רב יוסף. Then the גמרא begins רב יוסף's reply, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason she can't do יבום is that she would ruin the יבם's home, the same worry applies to any new husband. But the very same פסוק says she 'becomes another man's.' So the reason seems to prove too much, and רב יוסף must explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: To another man

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if so,
she should not marry another man either,
so that she not destroy his house!
phrases.notes: Here "his house" means the new husband's home.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף's answer comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לְאַחֵר לָא תִּינָּשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in the second version (step 12).
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'so that she not destroy the house' reason for blocking יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason would equally forbid her to any new husband, yet the פסוק itself permits her to 'another man.'
